capabilities: Prompt for a name and vault folder when an outside note opens
Copy the note into the vault and switch the tab to the copy
Move the original file to the system Trash
Skip notes from other vaults and ignore chosen folders
Import from the status bar, tab menu or a command
disambiguation: Not a converter for other apps' note formats; it only copies Markdown files you already opened in Obsidian into the vault.
extras: Desktop only and requires Obsidian 1.14.4 or later; the README notes it can be installed with BRAT before it is listed in the directory. It reads and moves files outside the vault but only ones the user opened, never deletes permanently and makes no network requests. Images linked with relative paths next to the original are not copied yet.
intentEvidence: Since 1.14.4, Obsidian can open a Markdown file from Finder or Explorer even when it isn't in your vault.
motivation: The author wanted to catch the moment an outside note opens in Obsidian and bring it into the vault, since such notes are never indexed and are easy to lose track of once the tab is closed.
problem: Markdown files opened from outside the vault appear in a tab but are never indexed, so they are missing from search, links and the file list and are easy to lose.
summary: Prompt that copies a Markdown file opened from outside the vault into a chosen vault folder and moves the original to the Trash.
